title: Personal Credit Cards: closing autopay amount never above the last statement balance
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: last statement balance as the ceiling of a closing autopay

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder closing a card that will still carry a balance records a closing fixed-amount autopay instruction, it limits the fixed amount by the card's last statement balance.

## Rule

1. The fixed amount of the closing autopay is never more than the card's last statement balance.
2. When the balance owed counted from the ledger is above the last statement balance, the last statement balance is used instead.
3. When the ledger balance owed is at or below the last statement balance, the ledger figure stands.

## Comparison table (hypothetical figures)

| Ledger balance owed | Last statement balance | Figure carried forward |
|---|---|---|
| 1480.25 USD | 1300.00 USD | 1300.00 USD, the last statement balance |
| 900.10 USD | 1300.00 USD | 900.10 USD, the ledger figure |
| 1300.00 USD | 1300.00 USD | 1300.00 USD, either figure |

## Points of judgement

- New purchases or interest posted since the last statement can lift the ledger figure above the last statement balance; the ceiling then applies.
- The ceiling is the card's own last statement balance, not the minimum payment due on that statement.
